lesson:
Cox proportional hazards regression serves as the standard multivariable approach in prognostic research [E-001]. Model validity requires evaluating the proportional hazards (PH) assumption using scaled Schoenfeld residuals; violations are handled using stratified Cox models or time-varying coefficient models [E-001, E-003]. To prevent model overfitting, estimation bias, and inflated type I error, models must maintain adequate events per variable (EPV) [E-001, E-002]. While 10 to 20 EPV is the standard benchmark, an EPV between 5 and 9 can be acceptable under certain conditions if key confounders are adequately controlled [E-002]. Because categorical covariates such as stage and grade utilize indicator coding, each category consumes degrees of freedom and requires a proportional increase in observed events [E-001, E-002]. Furthermore, REMARK guidelines advise against data-driven categorization of continuous variables [E-001]. Continuous predictors and markers should retain their continuous scale, using restricted cubic splines or fractional polynomials to accommodate non-linear functional forms without information loss or misclassification [E-001, E-004].

Key facts:
* The proportional hazards assumption must be verified using scaled Schoenfeld residuals, and any violations should be addressed via stratified Cox models or time-varying coefficient models [E-001, E-003].
* While 10 to 20 events per variable (EPV) is standard to prevent severe bias and inflated type I error, an EPV of 5 to 9 can be acceptable under specific conditions if key confounders are adequately controlled [E-001, E-002].
* Continuous predictors should avoid data-driven cutpoints and instead be modeled continuously using fractional polynomials or restricted cubic splines to prevent information loss [E-001, E-004].
* Categorical covariates, such as stage and grade, require indicator coding across levels, where each indicator consumes degrees of freedom and demands proportional increases in total event counts [E-001, E-002].

sources.title: Reporting Recommendations for Tumor Marker Prognostic Studies (REMARK): Explanation and Elaboration
sources.finding: Provides consensus guidelines stipulating that multivariable survival models must specify candidate variables, evaluate and address proportional hazards assumptions, preserve continuous marker data rather than using data-driven cutpoints, and ensure adequate event counts to avoid overfitting.

sources.title: Relaxing the Rule of Ten Events per Variable in Logistic and Cox Regression
sources.finding: Demonstrates that while 10 to 20 events per variable (EPV) is standard to prevent severe bias and inflated type I error in Cox proportional hazards regression, EPV values between 5 and 9 can be acceptable under certain conditions if key confounders are adequately controlled.

sources.title: Variables with Time-Varying Effects and the Cox Model: Some Statistical Concepts Illustrated with a Prognostic Factor Study in Breast Cancer
sources.finding: Details methodology for diagnosing non-proportional hazards using scaled Schoenfeld residuals and demonstrates handling violated assumptions via stratified Cox models or time-varying coefficient models.

sources.title: Selection of Important Variables and Determination of Functional Form for Continuous Predictors in Multivariable Model Building
sources.finding: Establishes statistical frameworks for modeling continuous prognostic variables using fractional polynomials and restricted cubic splines to prevent information loss and misclassification induced by arbitrary categorizations.
